brief.claim: Among women whose menopausal symptom index at the start of the trial was at least 20 points, active hormone therapy lowers the index more than placebo does: the mean fall in the index (start minus week 12) is at least 3 points greater on active therapy than on placebo, and a one-sided Welch t test of that difference between the two arms is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: menopausal symptom index of each woman at the start of the trial (higher is worse)
symptom index of each woman at week 12
True if the woman was randomised to active hormone therapy, False if to placebo

brief.claim: In women treated for osteoporosis, first-year responders keep gaining more bone than first-year non-responders: women whose bone mineral density rose over the first year (from the start of treatment to the first 12-month scan) gain at least 0.5 percentage points more over the second year (percentage change from the second 12-month scan to the 24-month scan) than women whose density fell over the first year, and a one-sided Welch t test of that difference between the two groups of women is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: bone mineral density of each woman at the start of treatment (g/cm2)
bone mineral density at the 12-month visit, first of two scans taken at that visit (g/cm2)
bone mineral density at the 12-month visit, second of two scans taken at that visit (g/cm2)
bone mineral density at the 24-month visit (g/cm2)

brief.claim: Among patients whose first systolic blood-pressure reading was at least 160 mmHg, antihypertensive treatment lowers systolic pressure: the mean fall from the second reading (taken before treatment began) to the third reading (taken after 8 weeks of treatment) is at least 8 mmHg, and a one-sided paired t test of the fall is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: systolic blood pressure in mmHg; readings in time order: reading 1 at the screening visit, reading 2 at the pre-treatment visit, reading 3 after 8 weeks of treatment

brief.claim: In each participant's own region of visual cortex that responds more to faces than to houses, the response to faces exceeds the response to bodies: across the 12 participants the mean difference (faces minus bodies) of the response in that region is at least 0.3 percent signal change, and a one-sided paired t test across participants is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: response to face images (percent signal change) of each visual-cortex voxel in each scanning run of each participant
response to body images (percent signal change), same layout
response to house images (percent signal change), same layout

brief.claim: In the cortical voxels where participants respond to the task, the response is at least 0.25 percent signal change: the mean task effect, averaged over those voxels and across participants, is at least 0.25, and a one-sided one-sample t test across participants of the voxel-averaged effect is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: task effect (task minus rest, percent signal change) of each cortical voxel in each participant

brief.claim: In the voxels of this participant's visual cortex whose responses follow stimulus contrast, the response rises with contrast: the regression slope of the voxel-averaged response (percent signal change) on stimulus contrast across the 240 trials is at least 0.2 percent signal change per unit of contrast, with a one-sided p value below 0.05.

data_keys.meaning: response of each visual-cortex voxel on each trial, in percent signal change
stimulus contrast shown on each trial, in units where full contrast equals 1

brief.claim: Among the recorded visual neurons that fire more to vertical than to horizontal bars, the mean orientation index, (vertical minus horizontal) / (vertical plus horizontal) computed from trial-averaged firing rates, is at least 0.1.

data_keys.meaning: firing rate (spikes/s) of each neuron on each presentation of a vertical bar
firing rate (spikes/s) of each neuron on each presentation of a horizontal bar

brief.claim: Over the scalp electrodes that respond to the stimulus, the stimulus condition explains at least 10% of the variance of the electrode-averaged post-stimulus amplitude across trials (R-squared of at least 0.10 in a regression of that amplitude on the stimulus condition).

data_keys.meaning: mean post-stimulus EEG amplitude (microvolts) at each electrode on each trial
True on trials with the stimulus present, False on control trials

brief.claim: Across 16 participants, activation in the brain region whose response relates to the personality trait is correlated with the trait: the mean, over the voxels of that region, of the voxel-wise correlations (across participants) between activation and trait score is at least 0.5.

data_keys.meaning: activation of each voxel in each participant, measured in the first scanning session
activation of each voxel in each participant, measured in a second scanning session
questionnaire score on the personality trait for each participant

brief.claim: Neurons that are least active at rest increase their firing more with the manipulation than neurons that are most active at rest: ranking the 240 neurons by firing rate in the resting recording, the mean change in rate (post-manipulation minus pre-manipulation) of the lowest third exceeds that of the highest third by at least 1.0 spikes/s, and a one-sided Welch t test of that difference is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: firing rate (spikes/s) of each neuron in a resting recording
firing rate (spikes/s) of each neuron before the manipulation
firing rate (spikes/s) of each neuron after the manipulation

brief.claim: Patients show a larger evoked response than controls in the time window in which the two groups' responses differ: the mean amplitude over a window of 10 consecutive samples is at least 0.5 microvolts greater for patients than for controls, and a one-sided Welch t test of that difference is significant at the 0.05 level.

data_keys.meaning: evoked-response amplitude (microvolts) of each participant at each time sample after stimulus onset, time samples in order
True for a patient, False for a control participant

brief.claim: Among patients whose symptom score at the screening visit was at least 60, at least 40% improve by 10 points or more between the start of the programme and the 6-month follow-up (score at the start minus score at 6 months of at least 10); the claim is that the proportion of such patients is at least 0.40.

data_keys.meaning: symptom score of each patient at the screening visit (higher is worse)
symptom score of each patient at the start of the programme
symptom score of each patient at the 6-month follow-up
